title: The projective dimension of the residue field is at least dim m/m^2
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, and let $n=\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ (finite, as $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated). If $\kappa$, as an $R$-module, has a projective resolution $0\to P_d\to\dots\to P_0\to\kappa\to0$ of length $\le d$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] for an integer $d\ge0$, then $d\ge n$. Equivalently: $\operatorname{pd}_R\kappa\ge\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OA (lemma-length-resolution-residue-field, line 26966), with its proof (Koszul complex on a lift of a basis of m/m^2, minimal finite free resolution via Lemmas what-kind-of-resolutions-Noetherian-local and add-trivial-complex, comparison map by Lemma compare-resolutions, induction on the injectivity of alpha_i tensor kappa).
